extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners in technology/operations management and business/IP strategy (e.g., MBA students, corporate managers, IP professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study description of RPX Corporation's business and operating model for defending clients against patent trolls (NPEs), including how it acquires patents, sells its service, and captures value. Focuses on organizational teams, processes, and revenue/cost-capture mechanisms that enable a defensive patent-aggregation business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a strong customer need and devise a novel approach
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an example of an effective company because RPX not only identified a strong customer need but also devised a novel approach to addressing that need and then capturing some that value for itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company found a market inefficiency (costs and resource drain from patent trolls) and built a novel business model to address it; effectiveness requires both clear identification of customer pain and an innovative mechanism to capture value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use patents defensively to protect clients
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX seeks out and buys patents in order to use them defensively against patent trolls to protect its client base. It puts itself directly between NPEs and its clients as a first line of defensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive use includes countering patents held by NPEs during litigation or preempting litigation by acquiring relevant patents; the core product is defensive patent ownership rather than offensive licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and communicate cost savings to customers
rubrics_metrics.description: The company saves its customers the costs incurred from defending against litigation directly (by using its pool of patents...) so its customers can focus on innovation and creation of new tech and products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sales pitches should be highly quantitative, projecting specific dollar savings based on a prospective customer’s record with nuisance suits to demonstrate the value proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture value via an annual subscription fee
rubrics_metrics.description: In return, RPX captures a portion of those cost savings for itself by charging customers an annual subscription fee for its services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revenue model monetizes avoided costs through recurring subscription pricing rather than per-incident billing; this enables predictable capture of client value.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-mover/unique positioning in the defensive aggregator role
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX was the first and remains the only defensive patent aggregator in this space and has created a monopoly in protecting companies from patent trolls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being first and unique in the market can establish durable competitive advantage; structure the operating model to sustain that position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble a highly technical, consultative sales team
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX has assembled a highly technical sales team that is capable of a highly consultative sell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salespeople should be able to engage deeply with technically sophisticated clients, target companies embroiled in litigation, and present quantitative models that justify subscription costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target clients currently embroiled in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Salespeople are taught to target companies that are currently embroiled in litigation to offer RPX services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritizing firms facing active nuisance suits increases the immediacy and clarity of the value proposition and shortens sales cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a dedicated patent acquisition team with multi-disciplinary expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent acquisition team is comprised of financial, technical, and legal experts to assess the value and attractiveness of any individual patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-investment, cross-functional team is necessary to evaluate, price, and acquire patents; rigorous assessment helps ensure the purchased patents will be effective defensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustain significant patent-buying investment and a large patent pool
rubrics_metrics.description: The team spends over $100M every year and now sits on a pool of more than 10,000 patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale of purchasing matters: a large, diverse patent pool increases defensive coverage and bargaining leverage when countering NPEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate customer input into patent acquisition direction
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX allows its subscription customers to help determine the direction of future patent spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving customers influence over acquisition priorities aligns buys with client needs and increases perceived service value; smaller clients who pay less (insurance product) are excluded from this influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer tiered products (insurance for smaller clients)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a certain number of prospective clients that are too small to pay the subscription and therefore are offered the newer insurance product, which protects clients for a smaller fee and precludes them from influencing direction of spend on patent acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product segmentation allows broader market reach while preserving governance/decision rights for full subscribers; pricing and feature differentiation are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate consortium purchases through a business development team
rubrics_metrics.description: The business development team looks to coordinate multiple clients to collectively raise money (separate from the annual subscription) to buy large portfolios that RPX lacks resources to buy by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large portfolio acquisitions, pooling client funding reduces single-party exposure and enables purchases that expand defensive coverage; organizational capability to coordinate and structure such deals is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and acquire large patent portfolios as a strategic option
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond just looking at individual patents, RPX also evaluates large portfolios of patents for its clients... this has become a smaller piece of the larger subscription-based business model, further diversifying the business model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess portfolio-level value and coordinate acquisition financing; portfolio buys diversify defensive assets and can be integrated into subscription offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage patent pool to create additional revenue streams
rubrics_metrics.description: The company has since leveraged this pool of patents to create another small revenue stream to further diversify its business model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repurposing defensive assets (e.g., licensing or other monetization) can diversify revenue, but should be balanced against core defensive commitments to clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design an operating model of internal teams and processes to support strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: RPX has created several internal teams and processes to support its business model: Direct Sales, Patent Acquisition Team, Business Development Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating model alignment—specialized teams with clear responsibilities and processes—is necessary to deliver the defensive-aggregation value proposition at scale.
